features.title: Powerful Annotation Tools
features.sub: Everything you need. Nothing you don't.
feature.stepArrow.title: Step Arrow
feature.stepArrow.text: Arrows with auto-incrementing numbered circles — perfect for step-by-step guides.
feature.stepRectangle.title: Step Rectangle
feature.stepRectangle.text: Numbered rectangles that auto-increment — highlight regions with ordered callouts.
feature.arrow.title: Arrow Tool
feature.arrow.text: Draw clean, directional arrows with elegant filled arrowheads to point out details.
feature.rectangle.title: Rectangle
feature.rectangle.text: Highlight regions with outlined rectangles to draw attention to specific areas.
feature.ellipse.title: Circle / Ellipse
feature.ellipse.text: Draw circles and ellipses by dragging a bounding box. Stroke only, no fill.
feature.line.title: Line
feature.line.text: Draw simple straight lines without arrowheads.
feature.dashedLine.title: Dashed Line
feature.dashedLine.text: Draw straight dashed lines to mark borders, guides and boundaries. Right next to Line.
feature.questionArrow.title: Question Arrow
feature.questionArrow.text: Arrows with a question mark circle to mark questionable areas.
feature.questionRectangle.title: Question Rectangle
feature.questionRectangle.text: Rectangles with a question mark circle to mark questionable areas.
feature.exclamationArrow.title: Exclamation Arrow
feature.exclamationArrow.text: Arrows with an exclamation badge at the start — highlight warnings and must-see details.
feature.exclamationRectangle.title: Exclamation Rectangle
feature.exclamationRectangle.text: Rectangles with an exclamation badge at the top-left — call out critical regions.
feature.text.title: Text
feature.text.text: Place free-floating labels on the canvas — click to add, edit inline, and drag to reposition.
feature.abcArrow.title: ABC Arrow
feature.abcArrow.text: Arrows with auto-incrementing letter labels (a, b, ..., z, aa, ab).
feature.abcRectangle.title: ABC Rectangle
feature.abcRectangle.text: Rectangles with auto-incrementing letter labels (a, b, ..., z, aa, ab).
feature.magnifier.title: Magnifier
feature.magnifier.text: Create circular zoom lenses on your screenshot with configurable zoom (1.5×–5×). Perfect for highlighting small details.
feature.colorPicker.title: Color Picker
feature.colorPicker.text: Choose any annotation color with a full-spectrum color wheel.
feature.lineWidth.title: Line Width
feature.lineWidth.text: Adjust stroke thickness from 2px to 15px for just the right emphasis.
feature.areaSelection.title: Area Selection
feature.areaSelection.text: Select exactly the area you want to capture — no more cropping afterwards.
feature.saveCopy.title: Save & Copy
feature.saveCopy.text: One click saves to Downloads and copies to clipboard simultaneously.

verify.summary: How to check that your download really comes from us
verify.intro: Every FeatherShot release is built by GitHub Actions from the public source code. The files on GitHub and on our download mirror are exactly the same, so they have the same SHA-256 fingerprint. After each release, GitHub Actions also uploads every file to VirusTotal, where more than 60 antivirus engines check it. The results are added to the release notes.

press.metaDescription: FeatherShot brand assets, descriptions, and screenshots for press and marketing.
press.meta: Use these materials when writing about FeatherShot. MIT-licensed app; assets below are provided for editorial use.
press.shortText: FeatherShot is a fast, native screenshot annotation tool with arrows, numbered steps, callouts, and magnifier lenses — free and open source for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
press.longText: FeatherShot helps you capture a region of the screen and annotate it with professional tools: step arrows, numbered rectangles, text labels, question and exclamation callouts, ABC sequences, magnifier lenses, and flexible colors and stroke widths. It is lightweight, menu-bar friendly on macOS, and ships without subscriptions or cloud lock-in. Builds are available for macOS (native Swift), Windows and Linux (Electron), plus a Chrome extension for in-browser capture.
press.screenshotsText: Add product screenshots under hosting/public/marketing/screenshots/ in the repository. Until then, use the icon and website preview image below.
privacy.metaDescription: Privacy Policy for FeatherShot screenshot annotation apps on macOS, Windows, Linux, and Chrome.
privacy.meta: Last updated: March 22, 2026 · Applies to FeatherShot on macOS (including Mac App Store), Windows, Linux, and the Chrome extension.
privacy.intro: FeatherShot is developed by Kurt Steven Kainzmayer (“we”, “us”). This policy explains how the app handles information. FeatherShot is designed to work locally on your device. We do not operate user accounts and we do not sell personal data.
privacy.notCollectText: FeatherShot does not require sign-in. We do not collect names, email addresses, or payment information through the app. Screenshots and annotations you create stay on your device unless you choose to save, copy, or share them using system features (for example Finder, clipboard, or another app you open).
privacy.permCapture: Screen capture — Required to capture and annotate screen content. Capture happens on your device; we do not receive your screen images.
privacy.permFiles: Files and folders — Used when you save exports (for example to your Downloads folder).
privacy.permAccess: Accessibility or input — On some platforms, optional permissions may be requested only to support capture or global shortcuts. No content is transmitted to us.
privacy.networkText: Some builds may check whether a newer version is available by contacting GitHub (public release metadata only). This check does not include your screenshots or annotation data. You can use FeatherShot without creating a GitHub account. The desktop app may open our website or GitHub release pages when you choose “download update” or similar actions.
privacy.masText: If you install FeatherShot from the Mac App Store, distribution and updates are provided by Apple under Apple’s terms. Apple may process purchase and device information according to its own privacy policy. FeatherShot itself still does not collect analytics or personal data through our servers.
privacy.childrenText: FeatherShot is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.
privacy.retentionText: We do not store your screenshot content on our servers. Any files you save remain under your control on your device.
privacy.rightsText: If applicable law grants you rights to access, correct, or delete personal data, contact us below. Because we do not operate accounts or cloud storage for your captures, most requests will concern optional communications you send to us directly.
privacy.changesText: We may update this policy. The “Last updated” date at the top will change when we do. Continued use of the app after changes means you accept the updated policy.
privacy.contactText: Questions about privacy: GitHub Issues or email via the contact option on our GitHub profile.
support.metaDescription: Help and support for FeatherShot, the screenshot annotation app for macOS, Windows, Linux, and Chrome.
support.meta: FeatherShot is free and open source. This page answers the most common questions about the app on macOS, Windows, Linux, and the Chrome extension.
support.helpText: Report a bug, request a feature, or ask a question on GitHub Issues. When you report a problem, include your FeatherShot version (shown in the menu) and your macOS, Windows, or Linux version. On Windows and Linux, the tray menu’s Show Log File opens a log you can attach to the report.
support.screenRecordingText: FeatherShot needs Screen Recording permission to capture your screen. If a capture comes back empty or the selection does not appear, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording, turn FeatherShot on, and start the capture again. macOS may ask you to quit and reopen FeatherShot after you change this setting.
support.downloadsText: Save & Copy writes a timestamped PNG to your Downloads folder. macOS asks for permission the first time. If you declined, allow FeatherShot under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders. Copying to the clipboard works either way.
support.whereText: Saved screenshots are in your Downloads folder with a timestamp in the file name. Copies go to the clipboard, so you can paste them straight into another app. FeatherShot does not keep a copy on our servers, and it does not upload your screenshots anywhere.
support.shortcutsText: Every annotation tool has a shortcut that is shown in its tooltip (keys 1 to 0, -, =, T and M). ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z on Windows and Linux) undoes the last change, and ⌘S (Ctrl+S) saves and copies the screenshot. ⌘+, ⌘− and ⌘0 zoom in, zoom out, and show the screenshot at its original size. ⌘9 fits it to the window.
support.updatesText: The Mac App Store and TestFlight builds are updated by Apple. Downloads from GitHub and this website can check for a newer version from the menu. Each release is listed in the changelog.
support.privacyText: FeatherShot has no accounts and does not send your screenshots anywhere. Read the full privacy policy.
